entries.topic: South Lebanon 2026: the Forward Defense Line / Yellow Line, Israel's stated rationale, Lebanon's and the UN's positions, UNIFIL's end

claims.text: 19 Apr 2026: the Israeli military published its first public map of a 'Forward Defense Line' inside Lebanon, running roughly 5 to 10 km from the border and placing dozens of villages under Israeli control; military: 'Five divisions, alongside Israeli Navy forces, are operating simultaneously south of the forward defense line'; purpose to dismantle Hezbollah infrastructure and 'prevent direct threats to communities in northern Israel'; Katz said border homes Hezbollah exploits would be demolished; Lebanese authorities: >2,100 killed, >1.2m displaced since 2 March
28 Apr 2026, Foreign Minister Gideon Saar: 'Israel has no territorial ambitions in Lebanon'; 'Our presence in the areas by our northern border serves one purpose: protecting our citizens'

17 Oct 2026: Lebanese presidency said its military delegation would press for an 'end to Israeli attacks in Lebanon' at a trilateral meeting in Tampa on 20 Oct; under the US-brokered deal Beirut vowed to disarm Hezbollah and Israeli troops would gradually withdraw; Israeli forces remain on Lebanese land; Israel says its strikes respond to violations

UNSC resolution 2790, adopted unanimously 28 Aug 2025, extended UNIFIL a final time to 31 Dec 2026, followed by a one-year 'orderly and safe drawdown and withdrawal'; the US said Lebanese forces should take on more responsibility; France warned premature withdrawal could weaken the Lebanese government's efforts

Carnegie (Tokmajyan, 4 Dec 2025): 'the new order will be defined by reinforced boundaries and expanded buffer zones encircling Israel'; a ring of buffer zones replacing Iran's 'ring of fire'; south Lebanon's destroyed zone 'a wasteland that has functioned as a de facto buffer zone'; hard-line Israeli voices floated the Awali River as the boundary of a Hezbollah-free zone; Gaza ~1 km razed strip; Syria 'unlimited amount of time'; Israel's aim to 'push its adversaries away from its own borders'

entries.topic: Syria after Assad: the buffer zone, Mount Hermon, the demilitarisation demand, Sufa 53 and the responses

claims.text: 23 Feb 2025, IDF officers' graduation: Netanyahu: 'we demand the full demilitarization of southern Syria, in the Quneitra, Daraa, and As Suwayda provinces'; will not allow HTS or the new Syrian army south of Damascus; IDF had at least nine posts (two on Hermon, seven in the buffer zone); protests in Quneitra, Daraa and Suwayda followed; Syria's National Dialogue Conference warned against partition

Netanyahu 8 Dec 2024: 'We will not allow any hostile force to establish itself on our border'; 15 Dec 2024 announced a plan to double the Golan's population; 17 Dec 2024 visited the Hermon summit and said the IDF would stay 'until another solution ensuring Israel's security is found'; 9 Jan 2025 Israeli officials described a 15 km 'zone of control' and 60 km 'sphere of influence'; UN envoy Pedersen 20 Feb 2025 'the Israelis need to withdraw'; Guterres 25 Jul 2025 violations 'unacceptable and must cease'; Syria demands withdrawal to pre-8 Dec 2024 lines

5 Oct 2026: Qatar called Sufa 53 a 'flagrant breach of international principles'; Jordan said Israeli measures 'violated the UN Charter' and called for an end to the occupation of Syrian territory; Kuwait 'a dangerous escalation'; per SANA the berm runs from near Hader through Jubata al-Khashab and al-Hamidiya to al-Asha and the southern tri-point, begun mid-2022; a trench was dug southwest of al-Rafid; Syria said completing it breaches the 1974 agreement

UAE MFA 5 Oct 2026 condemned the 'resumption of excavation and bulldozing operations' in the area called the 'Sufa 53 line' and the construction of fortifications; 'categorical rejection of any violation of Syria's sovereignty'; breaches international law and the 1974 Disengagement Agreement

entries.topic: Gaza: the Yellow Line and orange line, share of the Strip over time, Israel's stated rationale, UN and Palestinian positions

claims.text: Trump 20-point plan (29 Sep 2025): point 3 'Israeli forces will withdraw to the agreed upon line'; 'battle lines will remain frozen until conditions are met for the complete staged withdrawal'; point 16 'Israel will not occupy or annex Gaza'; IDF to hand over territory to the ISF 'save for a security perimeter presence that will remain until Gaza is properly secure from any resurgent terror threat'

Al Jazeera 12 Oct 2026: OCHA estimated in 2010 the restricted area covered 17% of Gaza's land and 35% of its farmland; at the ceasefire Israel held 53% (Palestinians 47%, ~172 sq km); Forensic Architecture: 58% by December (2025); Israel told the UN in June it controls about 70%; OCHA: restrictions 'now cover 65 percent of Gaza'; ~35% (~128 sq km) left for 2.1 million; orange line maps sent to aid agencies in March; no Israeli rationale quoted
Al Jazeera 13 Oct 2026: on 11 Oct Israeli forces moved the yellow blocks several metres westward in Shujayea; Israel controls about 65% of Gaza according to the UN, up from 53% a year earlier

Al Jazeera 26 Jan 2026: Israeli military maps show roughly 58% of Gaza inside the area Israel holds ('nearly 60 percent'); OCHA: more than 70% of Gaza at various points under evacuation orders or unsafe

7 Dec 2025, chief of staff Eyal Zamir to reservists in Gaza (military statement): 'We have operational control over extensive parts of the Gaza Strip, and we will remain on those defense lines'; 'The Yellow Line is a new border line, serving as a forward defensive line for our communities'

Reuters 29 Apr 2026: maps sent to aid groups in mid-March show an 'orange line' restricted area covering an estimated 11% of Gaza beyond the Yellow Line; ARIJ's Jad Isaac: Israeli control at least 64%; COGAT: boundaries 'determined and updated in accordance with the operational situational assessment', zone to enable coordinated aid, civilians not affected; military: area adjacent to the line 'a sensitive and dangerous operational environment'; Israel has described territory it holds in Gaza, Syria and Lebanon as buffer zones against militant attacks; at least three Palestinians working with UN agencies killed between the lines

28 May 2026, Netanyahu at a conference in the West Bank (Channel 12 excerpts): 'Right now, we have Hamas by the throat'; 'We control 60% of the territory of the Strip'; control was 50% after the ceasefire; 'my directive is to go to 70'

12 Jun 2026, Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem: the line's westward movement aims to 'blow up the negotiation track'; 'blatant violation of the ceasefire agreement'; witnesses said blocks moved ~300 m west in Tuffah; Anadolu says Netanyahu acknowledged on 15 May ~60% with intent to reach 70%

UNSCO briefing 29 Jun 2026 (Alakbarov): 'Israel has said that it currently controls approximately 70% of the Gaza Strip'; Israeli forces expanding territorial control and areas requiring coordination, reducing civilian space

Wikipedia (Yellow Line): line ~45 km; yellow concrete blocks; berms from Dec 2025 (Forensic Architecture/Drop Site); BBC Verify found blocks in Tuffah moved ~295 m deeper between 27 Nov and 25 Dec 2025; AP (21 Jul 2026, Planet Labs imagery) reported berms over 23 km; IDF confirmed building the sand barrier (JPost 21 Jul 2026)
